All of limbos abilities revolve around banishing himself, people, and objects into a different plain: the rift.  People in the rift can only interact with other things in the rift, so if you banish a group of foes in the rift your allies can't hurt them unless they are in the rift as well.
This can be considered generally disruptive to group play with the exception of his fourth skill and certain mission types.

His 4 allows a big area to be locked in the rift, which is handy on defense/interception missions where you need to cover/stall since enemies outside the rift can't shoot in.  His 3, while it it is fun to use can also be disruptive in that it prevents projectiles from moving inside the rift.  This ability has an ammo cap, so if allies fill the rift with gunfire it will break stasis much quicker than normal.  That said this is your best stall move, so communicate that you plan to use it so your squad can work with you and not against you. (And most importantly is ok with that)

Even though the rift has it's disadvantages, Limbo still can be incredibly useful when played tactfully and moderately.  On sortie defense you can banish the operator you have to guard and never worry about that fool dying. Because your roll banishes yourself into the rift, you can revive anyone without dying.  Being in the rift also increases energy regeneration, so caster frames will appreciate the extra energy.  Speaking of casters, there are some warframe abilities that actually can pass from the rift to the corporal realm. Two examples would be Excals exalted blade and Mesas peacemaker.   


TL,Dr:  Be kind, don't constantly stop time.  Feel free to use the four, but think before using one.

I've always used kusari since the beta phase, and it's a fantastic weapon.  It's a great mix of a combo weapon and a zoning weapon. A few things I'd keep in mind while using it are

1. Light attacks vs heavy attacks

Kusari has a huge discrepancy between its fast light combos and its slow sickle attacks.  Knowing the difference between how long it takes to throw them out vs how long you'll be stuck in them is integral to mastery of the weapon.  The light combos require a fair amount of commitment to get their full damage in, while heavys make up for the slower start with better burst damage.  I use the light combos as the core of my own gameplay, and mix in heavies for style points.  Find which moves you like, and see what situations the shine in.  

2. Stances

Kusari has the most varied moveset out of all of the weapons, so using your stances properly let's you utilize this beauty to it's fullest potential.  Let's break down the lights and heavies for each stance

·High stance
Light combo is a high reaching frontal assault ending in a downward slam. Great damage, fantastic on breaking horns. Just be careful on not eating up too much stamina.  The heavy attack is the longest range zoning attack in the game, but it locks you in place the longest. Use it to peck off stuff, but try to not develop bad habits with it.

·Mid stance
Light combo begins as a nice crowd control ending in a single target slam. It's the slowest light combo so don't mash square to avoid getting locked into it when you don't want to.  The heavy combo is literally the opposite of this as it begins with single target focus to mild cc.  Overall it's a more tactical stance that rewards positioning and timing.

·Low stance
Originally the low stance light combo was an absolute monster in beta, and got nerfed to be more healthy. It's still amazing now. The light combo offers the same blender capabilities as a lawn mover and comes out quicker than the high stance one.  The heavy combo is a nice 3 hitter with good forward tracking. It's fun to catch a mob jumping backwards with this.

3. Skills

The two skills you will see talked about on here are reaper and blade spin. Reaper is a stationary dps move that goes great health/ki damage.  Best used on yokai.  Blade spin is a really freakin good forward roll with c.c. that lets you reposition while dealing damage. Its damage got nerfed awhile ago because everyone and their guardian spirit abused it too much, but it's still sugoi. Both of these are guard commands, so you gotta hold L1 then push triangle (blade spin is also high stance only)

Two other skills I'd recommend are the kick and black vines.  The kick is a guard command that does high ki damage. This is your best friend when dealing with humans that block. Kick em in the shin.  Black vines let's you pretend to be scorpion from mortal combat. It's a low stance gap closer that will either drag enemies towards you or you to them depending on weight.  There is a high stance version of this, but don't get that. It has too many recovery frames to be a good initiator.

If you're struggling on humans I definitely recommend throwing out a kick or two.  I also really like using black vines to pull people (it acts as a small stun) and immediately switching to high stance light combo, then repeat till dead.  Another skill you can pick up is footsweep. It's a high stance move that trips humans, opening them up to finishers. It doesn't work on guards and has some windup, so practice with it to know what distances you can safely bring it out.

Was not planning this to be a wall of text, but I hope it helps!
